result.summary: This PR enables hardware-accelerated SHA256 implementations (SSE4.1, AVX2, x86 SHA-NI) for MSVC builds on Windows, mirroring optimizations already available for GCC/Clang. It adds an MSVC implementation of GetCPUID and AVXEnabled using intrinsics (since MSVC lacks inline assembly on x64), and updates the CMake introspection checks to probe for these instruction sets under MSVC. Benchmarks show dramatic speedups, e.g. SHA256D64 dropping from ~11ns/byte to ~0.7-1.3ns/byte with SHA-NI on capable hardware.
result.problem: Before this PR, MSVC builds of Bitcoin Core used only the generic 'standard' SHA256 implementation, missing out on 5-10x speedups that GCC/Clang builds already get from SIMD and SHA extensions. Windows users and developers building with MSVC feel slower hashing performance across the node (block validation, mempool, PoW checks all use SHA256 heavily).

open_concerns: Project direction conflict: #31507 proposes moving away from MSVC support (using clang-cl instead), which runs counter to this PR's investment in MSVC-specific code (fanquake, 2026-08-12).
Maintainers (fanquake, maflcko) stated in August 2026 that the outcome of discussion (an IRC meeting referenced by hebasto) was to close this PR.
resolved_concerns: theuni's request to split out the ALWAYS_INLINE/inline-attribute refactor was addressed by extracting it into PR #27575, which merged.
fanquake's question about why GetCPUID was skipped for rdrand/rdseed on MSVC was clarified by sipa: rdrand/rdseed still need their own intrinsics implementation, unrelated to this PR's scope.
theuni's confusion about compat/cpuid.h double-definition and MSVC inline asm limitations was clarified by hebasto with compiler error evidence.
m3dwards's naming nit on a config symbol was acknowledged as non-blocking.

result.card: This PR enables hardware-accelerated SHA256 (SSE4.1, AVX2, SHA-NI) for MSVC/Windows builds, closing a long-standing gap where MSVC builds used only the slow generic SHA256 path while GCC/Clang builds already benefited from SIMD. Benchmarks from multiple reviewers (sipsorcery, achow101) show speedups of 5-10x, with SHA256D64 dropping from ~11ns/byte to under 1ns/byte on SHA-NI hardware, a substantial, real-world performance win for Windows users. The PR had strong technical support over its multi-year life (concept ACKs from laanwj and theuni, tested ACKs from sipsorcery) with only minor naming nits, but its future is now in doubt: maintainers fanquake and maflcko indicated in August 2026 that the discussed outcome favors closing this PR in favor of #31507, which moves toward dropping MSVC support entirely via clang-cl rather than extending MSVC-specific code. Review of the current code is likely moot until that direction is settled.
